newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LEHMAN, SINGH SHARE LEAD AT TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEHMAN, SINGH SHARE LEAD AT TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Tom Lehman and Vijay Singh both shot four-under-par rounds of 66 at Southern Hills on Thursday to share the first-round lead at the $3 million Tour Championship.

One stroke back was U.S. Open champion Steve Jones and current money list leader Phil Mickelson. Tiger Woods bogeyed the last hole to shoot a level par 70, a rare round out of the 60s for the tour's newest professional.
Both the money title and player of the year honours are on the line at the Tour Championship, the final event of the 1996 PGA Tour season.
Mickelson leads in both categories, but British Open champion Lehman can possibly edge him out with a win here.
Said Lehman, "I realise that second place for me doesn't mean anything - except a nice check - so I've come into this week thinking that way and really motivated."
Lehman said he was a bit disappointed with his round on Thursday, despite the fact that it left him in the lead.
"Golfers are never satisfied, but I played an extremely good round tee to green and missed a lot of putts," he said.
"I could have easily been five or six shots lower, which I know doesn't sound realistic on this golf course, but I played really well."

The top 30 money winners this year, who comprise the field in this exclusive event, all played quite well Thursday. Collectively they were 35 over par on this extremely difficult track, a number which seems high but is 50 strokes better than the field shot exactly one year ago at Southern Hills.
"Last year the course was so fast and firm it was frightening," said Lehman. "The rain earlier this week has softened it up just a bit to make it more playable."
Singh, who has had putting problems in recent months, and switched to the long putter at the start of the year, has gone back to a regular putter.
"I putted well, for a change," Singh said. "I've been working on my short game and it paid off. I should have changed back (to the short putter) earlier.
"It's kind of exciting to be out there hitting putts and knowing you're going to make them, and feeling like you couldn't wait to get on the greens."
The ultra long-hitting Woods, who has won two of the last three tournaments, failed to take advantage of the par-fives, as he usually does.

Southern Hills has just two par-fives, holes Woods ordinarily uses to separate himself from the field. But on Thursday Woods parred them both. It was not for lack of distance off the tee - Woods drove it 353 yards on the fifth hole and 347 yards on the 13th.

"This is completely different from the courses I've been playing for the last couple of months," said Woods. "It's an old style course, the kind I absolutely love. Par is a very good score here and I'm very happy to be in at even par."
